sections.label: 0 · 🧠 Mind World Models — Biological Origins & Foundational Definitions
path: 0 · 🧠 Mind World Models — Biological Origins & Foundational Definitions
sections.description: The concept of a "world model" originates in cognitive science and neuroscience. An agent's internal model of its environment allows it to predict sensory consequences of its own actions—the computational substrate of planning, imagination, and counterfactual reasoning. The papers below form the intellectual backbone of modern machine world models.

sections.label: 0.1 Foundational Cognitive & Neuroscientific Works
path: 0 · 🧠 Mind World Models — Biological Origins & Foundational Definitions
sections.description: Listed in chronological order, from Craik's 1943 "small-scale model" through the cognitive-map and predictive-coding traditions to Ha & Schmidhuber (2018) and LeCun's JEPA program (2022).

sections.label: 0.2 Formative Computational World Model Papers
path: 0 · 🧠 Mind World Models — Biological Origins & Foundational Definitions
sections.description: Listed in chronological order. This is the computational spine that §2.1 and §3.1 then scale: recurrent differentiable models (1990), Dyna-style imagination (1991), latent dynamics and action-conditional video (2011–2018), then RSSM/Dreamer (2019–2023).

sections.label: 1 · 🎨 Generative World Models
sections.description: Generative world models explicitly synthesize sensory observations (pixels, point clouds, tokens) of plausible futures conditioned on actions or language. Their primary value is as learned simulators and data augmenters.

sections.label: 1.1 🎮 Game & Interactive World Simulation
sections.description: These models simulate game environments frame-by-frame conditioned on player actions, essentially replacing traditional game engines with neural networks.

sections.label: 1.2 🚗 Autonomous Driving — Generative
sections.description: Generative driving world models synthesize future sensor observations (camera, LiDAR, radar) conditioned on ego trajectory, agent behaviors, weather, or language commands. They serve as learned simulators for data augmentation, safety evaluation, and closed-loop training.

sections.label: 1.3 🤖 Embodied AI & Robotics — Generative
sections.description: Generative world models in embodied AI simulate the visual or physical consequences of robot actions, enabling policy training in imagination and data-efficient learning. Subsections: manipulation (1.3.1), navigation (1.3.2), locomotion (1.3.3), VLA / WAM (1.3.4), and Real2Sim (1.3.5).

sections.label: 1.3.4 World-Model-Based Vision-Language-Action (VLA) & World Action Models (WAM)
sections.description: World Action Models jointly predict futures and actions in one backbone, often initialized from video generation. This subsection also includes VLAs with an explicit world-model head, latent-action pretraining from action-free video, and predict-then-act image-editing planners. Generic VLAs that map observation + language directly to actions without a dynamics component are out of scope — see Definition and Scope and the VLA vs. WAM glossary entry.

notes.title: WAM survey cross-audit additions
notes.text: The following entries were missing from this README but are part of the 109-paper WAM survey collection. They are kept in a separate audit block so the broader WAM boundary remains explicit.

sections.label: 1.3.5 Real2Sim & Structured Embodied World Construction
sections.description: These systems construct executable physical-world representations, simulation-ready twins, or structured intermediate state interfaces for embodied learning and evaluation.

sections.label: 1.4 🌐 3D / 4D Scene Generation
sections.description: Models that generate three-dimensional or four-dimensional (spatial + temporal) world representations, typically as explorable environments.

sections.label: 1.5 🔬 Scientific & Physical World Modeling
sections.description: World models that simulate physical, biological, or earth-science processes rather than human-scale scenes.

sections.label: 1.6 🎞️ General Video World Models & Rollout Backbones
path: 1.6 🎞️ General Video World Models & Rollout Backbones
sections.description: Video foundation models and rollout recipes that are repeatedly used as the backbone for interactive, embodied, or long-horizon world models. Generic video generation is still filtered out unless the paper explicitly targets control, causality, memory, or world-model conversion.

sections.label: 1.7 🎬 Persistent Narrative & Multi-Shot Video World Models
path: 1.7 🎬 Persistent Narrative & Multi-Shot Video World Models
sections.description: Every video generator implicitly models visual dynamics, but implicit dynamics alone are below the bar here. An entry needs documented state, memory, or structured planning that crosses a chunk/shot/scene boundary, plus continued prediction from that state, intervention on the ongoing rollout, or evaluation of its downstream use. Streaming has a higher interactivity ceiling only when the system accepts new input after a generated prefix is already available; autoregression, generation speed, identity consistency, or full-sequence attention alone does not suffice — nor does video length, visual quality, or multi-shot output. Methods whose primary contribution is generic causal/streaming rollout machinery live in §1.6; entries that overlap both are placed by primary contribution.

sections.label: 2 · 🏗️ Representational World Models
sections.description: Representational world models learn structured internal state representations without necessarily generating pixel-faithful observations. The emphasis is on encoding abstract, task-relevant features sufficient for planning and prediction.

sections.label: 2.1 Latent Dynamics Models (RSSM / Dreamer Family)
sections.description: Separate the world into deterministic and stochastic latent components; predict future latent states without decoding to pixels.

sections.label: 2.2 Joint Embedding Predictive Architectures (JEPA)
sections.description: Instead of generating observations, JEPA models predict abstract representations of future states. Inspired by LeCun's energy-based formulation.

sections.label: 2.3 Occupancy & BEV Representations
sections.description: Structured 3D world representations encoding semantic and geometric information for autonomous agents.

sections.label: 2.4 Multimodal, Text, Acoustic & Memory-Oriented World Models
path: 2.4 Multimodal, Text, Acoustic & Memory-Oriented World Models

sections.label: 3 · 🤖 Agentic World Models
sections.description: Agentic world models combine a world foundation model with an agentic decision-making framework. They enable an AI system to act, plan, and reason using its internal world model — essentially the realization of LeCun's autonomous machine intelligence architecture.

entries.name: Primate Vision and Predictive Models
entries.fullTitle: Primate vision reveals a missing principle for robust dynamic AI
entries.description: Compares predictive world-model representations with human behavior and macaque cortex, identifying strengths in appearance-invariant motion coding and a remaining temporal-integration gap.
entries.citation: Primate Vision and Predictive Models — "Primate vision reveals a missing principle for robust dynamic AI." arXiv 2608.23790 (2026).
categoryPath: 0 · 🧠 Mind World Models — Biological Origins & Foundational Definitions

entries.name: The Nature of Explanation (Craik)
entries.fullTitle: The Nature of Explanation
entries.description: Origin of the concept. First articulation that organisms carry a "small-scale model" of external reality in their heads, enabling them to try out alternatives and react to future situations before they arise.
entries.citation: The Nature of Explanation (Craik) — Craik, K.J.W. The Nature of Explanation. Cambridge University Press (1943).
categoryPath: 0 · 🧠 Mind World Models — Biological Origins & Foundational Definitions

entries.name: Cognitive Maps in Rats and Men (Tolman)
entries.fullTitle: Cognitive Maps in Rats and Men
entries.description: Classic behavioral evidence that animals learn map-like internal representations of the environment rather than mere stimulus-response chains — the ancestral "world model" in psychology.
entries.citation: Cognitive Maps in Rats and Men (Tolman) — Tolman, E.C. "Cognitive Maps in Rats and Men." Psychological Review 55(4):189–208 (1948).
categoryPath: 0 · 🧠 Mind World Models — Biological Origins & Foundational Definitions

entries.name: The Hippocampus as a Cognitive Map
entries.fullTitle: The Hippocampus as a Cognitive Map
entries.description: Landmark neuroscience synthesis identifying the hippocampus (place cells) as the neural substrate of Tolman's cognitive map; foundation for spatial world-model research.
entries.citation: The Hippocampus as a Cognitive Map — O'Keefe, J. & Nadel, L. The Hippocampus as a Cognitive Map. Oxford University Press (1978).
categoryPath: 0 · 🧠 Mind World Models — Biological Origins & Foundational Definitions

entries.name: Mental Models (Johnson-Laird)
entries.fullTitle: Mental Models: Towards a Cognitive Science of Language, Inference, and Consciousness
entries.description: Cognitive-science theory that reasoning operates over constructed internal models of situations rather than formal logic rules — a direct intellectual ancestor of "mental world modeling."
entries.citation: Mental Models (Johnson-Laird) — Johnson-Laird, P.N. Mental Models: Towards a Cognitive Science of Language, Inference, and Consciousness. Harvard University Press (1983).
categoryPath: 0 · 🧠 Mind World Models — Biological Origins & Foundational Definitions

entries.name: Occupancy Grids
entries.fullTitle: Using Occupancy Grids for Mobile Robot Perception and Navigation
entries.description: First computational formalization of a spatial world model for a physical agent.
entries.citation: Occupancy Grids — Elfes, A. "Using Occupancy Grids for Mobile Robot Perception and Navigation." Computer (1989).
categoryPath: 0 · 🧠 Mind World Models — Biological Origins & Foundational Definitions

entries.name: Successor Representations
entries.fullTitle: Improving Generalization for Temporal Difference Learning: The Successor Representation
entries.description: Foundational representation: encode the future occupancy of states rather than immediate reward.
entries.citation: Successor Representations — Dayan, P. "Improving Generalization for Temporal Difference Learning: The Successor Representation." Neural Computation (1993).
categoryPath: 0 · 🧠 Mind World Models — Biological Origins & Foundational Definitions

entries.name: Internal Models for Sensorimotor Integration
entries.fullTitle: An Internal Model for Sensorimotor Integration
entries.description: Canonical evidence that the brain uses forward models to predict sensory consequences of motor commands — the neuroscience blueprint for action-conditioned prediction.
entries.citation: Internal Models for Sensorimotor Integration — Wolpert, D.M., Ghahramani, Z. & Jordan, M.I. "An Internal Model for Sensorimotor Integration." Science 269(5232):1880–1882 (1995).
categoryPath: 0 · 🧠 Mind World Models — Biological Origins & Foundational Definitions

entries.name: Predictive Coding in the Visual Cortex
entries.fullTitle: Predictive Coding in the Visual Cortex: A Functional Interpretation of Some Extra-Classical Receptive-Field Effects
entries.description: The concrete computational predictive-coding model (predating Friston's free-energy generalization): higher cortical areas predict lower-level activity and feed back prediction errors.
entries.citation: Predictive Coding in the Visual Cortex — Rao, R.P.N. & Ballard, D.H. "Predictive Coding in the Visual Cortex: A Functional Interpretation of Some Extra-Classical Receptive-Field Effects." Nature Neuroscience 2:79–87 (1999).
categoryPath: 0 · 🧠 Mind World Models — Biological Origins & Foundational Definitions

entries.name: Predictive Coding / Free Energy Principle
entries.fullTitle: The free-energy principle: a unified brain theory?
entries.description: Neuro-scientific grounding: the brain as a hierarchical Bayesian inference machine minimizing prediction error.
entries.citation: Predictive Coding / Free Energy Principle — Friston, K. "The free-energy principle: a unified brain theory?" Nature Reviews Neuroscience (2010).
categoryPath: 0 · 🧠 Mind World Models — Biological Origins & Foundational Definitions

entries.name: Mental Simulation / Theory of Mind
entries.fullTitle: Simulation as an engine of physical scene understanding
entries.description: Humans use fast approximate physics simulators as a world model for intuitive physics.
entries.citation: Mental Simulation / Theory of Mind — Battaglia, P. et al. "Simulation as an engine of physical scene understanding." PNAS (2013).
categoryPath: 0 · 🧠 Mind World Models — Biological Origins & Foundational Definitions

entries.name: World Models (Ha & Schmidhuber)
entries.fullTitle: World Models
entries.description: Seminal work. Learn a compressed (V) perception model + recurrent (M) world model, train a small controller (C) entirely inside imagination. Introduced MDN-RNN for stochastic world model.
entries.citation: World Models (Ha & Schmidhuber) — Ha, D. & Schmidhuber, J. "World Models." arXiv 1803.10122 (2018).
categoryPath: 0 · 🧠 Mind World Models — Biological Origins & Foundational Definitions

entries.name: A Path Towards Autonomous Machine Intelligence (LeCun)
entries.fullTitle: A Path Towards Autonomous Machine Intelligence
entries.description: Proposes a modular architecture centered on a Joint Embedding Predictive Architecture (JEPA) world model for energy-efficient reasoning without pixel-level generation.
entries.citation: A Path Towards Autonomous Machine Intelligence (LeCun) — LeCun, Y. "A Path Towards Autonomous Machine Intelligence." OpenReview (2022).
categoryPath: 0 · 🧠 Mind World Models — Biological Origins & Foundational Definitions

entries.name: Making the World Differentiable (Schmidhuber)
entries.fullTitle: Making the World Differentiable: On Using Self-Supervised Fully Recurrent Neural Networks for Dynamic Reinforcement Learning and Planning in Non-Stationary Environments
entries.description: The 1990 recurrent controller–model architecture cited by Ha & Schmidhuber (2018) as the direct ancestor of learned neural world models for planning.
entries.citation: Making the World Differentiable (Schmidhuber) — Schmidhuber, J. "Making the World Differentiable: On Using Self-Supervised Fully Recurrent Neural Networks for Dynamic Reinforcement Learning and Planning in Non-Stationary Environments." TR FKI-126-90, TU Munich (1990).
categoryPath: 0 · 🧠 Mind World Models — Biological Origins & Foundational Definitions

entries.name: Dyna (Sutton)
entries.fullTitle: Dyna, an Integrated Architecture for Learning, Planning, and Reacting
entries.description: Foundational MBRL architecture. Interleaves real experience with simulated experience from a learned model — the template behind MBPO-style rollouts and modern "Dyna-style" agents.
entries.citation: Dyna (Sutton) — Sutton, R.S. "Dyna, an Integrated Architecture for Learning, Planning, and Reacting." ACM SIGART Bulletin 2(4):160–163 (1991).
categoryPath: 0 · 🧠 Mind World Models — Biological Origins & Foundational Definitions

entries.name: PILCO
entries.fullTitle: PILCO: A Model-Based and Data-Efficient Approach to Policy Search
entries.description: Gaussian-process dynamics model with analytic uncertainty propagation; long-standing reference point for data-efficient model-based policy search.
entries.citation: PILCO — Deisenroth, M.P. & Rasmussen, C.E. "PILCO: A Model-Based and Data-Efficient Approach to Policy Search." ICML 2011.
categoryPath: 0 · 🧠 Mind World Models — Biological Origins & Foundational Definitions

entries.name: Embed to Control (E2C)
entries.fullTitle: Embed to Control: A Locally Linear Latent Dynamics Model for Control from Raw Images
entries.description: Early latent dynamics model learned from pixels with locally linear transitions enabling optimal control in latent space — a precursor of PlaNet-style latent planning.
entries.citation: Embed to Control (E2C) — Watter, M. et al. "Embed to Control: A Locally Linear Latent Dynamics Model for Control from Raw Images." NeurIPS 2015.
categoryPath: 0 · 🧠 Mind World Models — Biological Origins & Foundational Definitions

entries.name: Action-Conditional Video Prediction
entries.fullTitle: Action-Conditional Video Prediction using Deep Networks in Atari Games
entries.description: First deep action-conditioned video prediction at scale (Atari); established the action-conditional next-frame formulation used by generative world models today.
entries.citation: Action-Conditional Video Prediction — Oh, J. et al. "Action-Conditional Video Prediction using Deep Networks in Atari Games." NeurIPS 2015.
categoryPath: 0 · 🧠 Mind World Models — Biological Origins & Foundational Definitions

entries.name: Successor Features
entries.fullTitle: Successor Features for Transfer in Reinforcement Learning
entries.description: Generalizes Dayan's successor representation to deep features; decouples environment dynamics from rewards for transfer — a key representational world-model idea.
entries.citation: Successor Features — Barreto, A. et al. "Successor Features for Transfer in Reinforcement Learning." NeurIPS 2017.
categoryPath: 0 · 🧠 Mind World Models — Biological Origins & Foundational Definitions

entries.name: Value Prediction Network (VPN)
entries.fullTitle: Value Prediction Network
entries.description: Plans with an abstract model that predicts future values and rewards rather than future observations — direct precursor of MuZero's value-equivalent world model.
entries.citation: Value Prediction Network (VPN) — Oh, J., Singh, S. & Lee, H. "Value Prediction Network." NeurIPS 2017.
categoryPath: 0 · 🧠 Mind World Models — Biological Origins & Foundational Definitions

entries.name: Imagination-Augmented Agents (I2A)
entries.fullTitle: Imagination-Augmented Agents for Deep Reinforcement Learning
entries.description: Learns to interpret imperfect learned-model rollouts as additional context for a model-free policy — an early, influential template for "imagination" in agents.
entries.citation: Imagination-Augmented Agents (I2A) — Racanière, S., Weber, T. et al. "Imagination-Augmented Agents for Deep Reinforcement Learning." NeurIPS 2017.
categoryPath: 0 · 🧠 Mind World Models — Biological Origins & Foundational Definitions

entries.name: Temporal Difference Models (TDM)
entries.fullTitle: Temporal Difference Models: Model-Free Deep RL for Model-Based Control
entries.description: Bridges model-free and model-based RL: goal-conditioned value functions trained model-free act as implicit horizon-varying dynamics models for planning.
entries.citation: Temporal Difference Models (TDM) — Pong, V., Gu, S., Dalal, M. & Levine, S. "Temporal Difference Models: Model-Free Deep RL for Model-Based Control." ICLR 2018.
categoryPath: 0 · 🧠 Mind World Models — Biological Origins & Foundational Definitions

entries.name: Generative Query Networks (GQN)
entries.fullTitle: Neural Scene Representation and Rendering
entries.description: Learns implicit 3D scene representations from posed observations and renders unseen viewpoints — formative for viewpoint-consistent neural scene world models.
entries.citation: Generative Query Networks (GQN) — Eslami, S.M.A. et al. "Neural Scene Representation and Rendering." Science 360(6394):1204–1210 (2018).
categoryPath: 0 · 🧠 Mind World Models — Biological Origins & Foundational Definitions

entries.name: Recurrent World Models Facilitate Policy Evolution
entries.fullTitle: Recurrent World Models Facilitate Policy Evolution
entries.description: Conference version of World Models (§0.1): V-M-C trained entirely in imagination, with evolution of a compact controller inside the MDN-RNN dream.
entries.citation: Recurrent World Models Facilitate Policy Evolution — Ha, D. & Schmidhuber, J. NeurIPS 2018.
categoryPath: 0 · 🧠 Mind World Models — Biological Origins & Foundational Definitions

entries.name: Learning Latent Dynamics for Planning (PlaNet)
entries.fullTitle: Learning Latent Dynamics for Planning from Pixels
entries.description: Introduced RSSM (Recurrent State-Space Model): separate deterministic and stochastic latent paths; latent-space cross-entropy planning.
entries.citation: Learning Latent Dynamics for Planning (PlaNet) — Hafner, D. et al. ICML 2019.
categoryPath: 0 · 🧠 Mind World Models — Biological Origins & Foundational Definitions

entries.name: Learning to Predict Without Looking Ahead
entries.fullTitle: Learning to Predict Without Looking Ahead: World Models Without Forward Prediction
entries.description: Uses observational dropout during reinforcement learning to induce an internal world model that fills gaps in observations, without an explicit supervised forward-prediction objective.
entries.citation: Learning to Predict Without Looking Ahead — Freeman, C. D., Metz, L. & Ha, D. "Learning to Predict Without Looking Ahead: World Models Without Forward Prediction." NeurIPS 2019.
categoryPath: 0 · 🧠 Mind World Models — Biological Origins & Foundational Definitions

entries.name: SimPLe
entries.fullTitle: Model-Based Reinforcement Learning for Atari
entries.description: First demonstration that a learned video-prediction world model supports sample-efficient Atari agents (~100k interactions); origin of the Atari 100k evaluation protocol.
entries.citation: SimPLe — Kaiser, Ł. et al. "Model-Based Reinforcement Learning for Atari." ICLR 2020.
categoryPath: 0 · 🧠 Mind World Models — Biological Origins & Foundational Definitions

entries.name: Dream to Control (Dreamer)
entries.fullTitle: Dream to Control: Learning Behaviors by Latent Imagination
entries.description: Actor-critic entirely trained in latent-dream world; strong Atari & continuous control benchmark results.
entries.citation: Dream to Control (Dreamer) — Hafner, D. et al. ICLR 2020.
categoryPath: 0 · 🧠 Mind World Models — Biological Origins & Foundational Definitions

entries.name: The Value Equivalence Principle
entries.fullTitle: The Value Equivalence Principle for Model-Based Reinforcement Learning
entries.description: Formalizes when a world model only needs to be accurate for value prediction rather than observation reconstruction — theoretical backbone of MuZero-style models.
entries.citation: The Value Equivalence Principle — Grimm, C., Barreto, A., Singh, S. & Silver, D. "The Value Equivalence Principle for Model-Based Reinforcement Learning." NeurIPS 2020.
categoryPath: 0 · 🧠 Mind World Models — Biological Origins & Foundational Definitions

entries.name: Mastering Atari with Discrete World Models (DreamerV2)
entries.fullTitle: Mastering Atari with Discrete World Models
entries.description: Discrete latent variables via straight-through gradients; matches Rainbow DQN with no environment interaction during policy training.
entries.citation: Mastering Atari with Discrete World Models (DreamerV2) — Hafner, D. et al. ICLR 2021.
categoryPath: 0 · 🧠 Mind World Models — Biological Origins & Foundational Definitions

entries.name: Dual Stream World Model (DSWM)
entries.fullTitle: A Biologically-Inspired Dual Stream World Model
entries.description: Separates visual observations into context and content streams inspired by the medial temporal lobe, generating imagined trajectories after one exposure and supporting policy learning through Dyna-like updates.
entries.citation: Dual Stream World Model (DSWM) — Juliani, A. & Sereno, M. "A Biologically-Inspired Dual Stream World Model." arXiv 2022.
categoryPath: 0 · 🧠 Mind World Models — Biological Origins & Foundational Definitions

entries.name: Mastering Diverse Domains with World Models (DreamerV3)
entries.fullTitle: Mastering Diverse Domains through World Models
entries.description: Single fixed hyperparameter set generalizing across continuous control, Atari, DMLab, Minecraft, ProcGen, and BSuite.
entries.citation: Mastering Diverse Domains with World Models (DreamerV3) — Hafner, D. et al. (2023).
categoryPath: 0 · 🧠 Mind World Models — Biological Origins & Foundational Definitions

entries.name: GameNGen
entries.fullTitle: Diffusion Models Are Real-Time Game Engines
entries.description: First real-time neural game engine simulating DOOM at >20 FPS; diffusion model conditioned on action history.
entries.citation: GameNGen — Valevski, D. et al. "Diffusion Models Are Real-Time Game Engines." arXiv 2408.14837 (2024).

entries.name: DIAMOND
entries.fullTitle: Diffusion for World Modeling: Visual Details Matter in Atari
entries.description: Diffusion-based world model trained on Atari achieving state-of-the-art imagination quality; highlights visual fidelity for downstream RL.
entries.citation: DIAMOND — Alonso, E. et al. "Diffusion for World Modeling: Visual Details Matter in Atari." NeurIPS 2024.

entries.name: Matrix-Game
entries.fullTitle: Matrix-Game: Interactive World Foundation Model
entries.description: Open-source interactive world foundation model for gaming; controllable action-conditioned video generation.
entries.citation: Matrix-Game — "Matrix-Game: Interactive World Foundation Model." arXiv 2506.18701 (2025).

entries.name: Matrix-Game 2.0
entries.fullTitle: Matrix-Game 2.0: An Open-Source, Real-Time, and Streaming Interactive World Model
entries.description: Streaming real-time extension with improved consistency and interactivity.
entries.citation: Matrix-Game 2.0 — "Matrix-Game 2.0: An Open-Source, Real-Time, and Streaming Interactive World Model." arXiv 2508.13009 (2025).

entries.name: A Frame is Worth One Token
entries.fullTitle: A Frame is Worth One Token: Efficient Generative World Modeling with Delta Tokens
entries.description: Compresses frame-to-frame change into delta tokens — a practical direction for cheaper long-horizon rollout.
entries.citation: A Frame is Worth One Token — "A Frame is Worth One Token: Efficient Generative World Modeling with Delta Tokens." arXiv 2604.04913 (2026).

entries.name: Neural Game Engine
entries.fullTitle: Neural Game Engine: Accurate learning of generalizable forward models from pixels
entries.description: Coined the "neural game engine" framing: learns pixel-level forward models of GVGAI games (with reward prediction) that generalize to unseen level sizes and plug into MCTS and model-based RL.
entries.citation: Neural Game Engine — Bamford, C. & Lucas, S. "Neural Game Engine: Accurate learning of generalizable forward models from pixels." arXiv 2003.10520 (2020).

entries.name: GameGAN
entries.fullTitle: Learning to Simulate Dynamic Environments with GameGAN
entries.description: GAN-era neural game engine (Pac-Man) that renders the next screen from key presses, with a memory module building an internal environment map and disentangled static/dynamic components.
entries.citation: GameGAN — Kim, S.W. et al. "Learning to Simulate Dynamic Environments with GameGAN." CVPR 2020.

entries.name: GameGen-X
entries.fullTitle: GameGen-X: Interactive Open-world Game Video Generation
entries.description: Diffusion transformer for open-world game video that predicts and alters future content from the current clip via InstructNet control experts, trained on the 1M-clip OGameData corpus from 150+ games.
entries.citation: GameGen-X — Che, H. et al. "GameGen-X: Interactive Open-world Game Video Generation." arXiv 2411.00769 (2024).

entries.name: PlayGen
entries.fullTitle: Playable Game Generation
entries.description: Autoregressive DiT-based diffusion game engine with a playability-based evaluation framework; sustains real-time interactive mechanics simulation past 1000 frames on an RTX 2060.
entries.citation: PlayGen — Yang, M. et al. "Playable Game Generation." arXiv 2412.00887 (2024).

entries.name: The Matrix
entries.fullTitle: The Matrix: Infinite-Horizon World Generation with Real-Time Moving Control
entries.description: Trained on AAA games (Forza Horizon 5, Cyberpunk 2077) plus real footage, it streams hour-long 720p rollouts at 16 FPS with real-time movement control and zero-shot game-to-real transfer.
entries.citation: The Matrix — Feng, R. et al. "The Matrix: Infinite-Horizon World Generation with Real-Time Moving Control." arXiv 2412.03568 (2024).

entries.name: Next-Frame Diffusion
entries.fullTitle: Playing with Transformer at 30+ FPS via Next-Frame Diffusion
entries.description: Block-wise causal diffusion transformer with consistency distillation and action-aware speculative sampling, reaching 30+ FPS action-conditioned Minecraft generation on a single A100.
entries.citation: Next-Frame Diffusion — Cheng, X. et al. "Playing with Transformer at 30+ FPS via Next-Frame Diffusion." arXiv 2506.01380 (2025).

entries.name: PlayerOne
entries.fullTitle: PlayerOne: Egocentric World Simulator
entries.description: Egocentric world simulator driven by the user's real body motion (part-disentangled motion injection) with joint 4D-scene/video reconstruction to keep the simulated world consistent over long rollouts.
entries.citation: PlayerOne — Tu, Y. et al. "PlayerOne: Egocentric World Simulator." arXiv 2506.09995 (2025).

entries.name: Hunyuan-GameCraft
entries.fullTitle: Hunyuan-GameCraft: High-dynamic Interactive Game Video Generation with Hybrid History Condition
entries.description: Unifies keyboard/mouse input into a shared camera-action space and extends rollouts autoregressively with hybrid history conditioning; distilled for real-time play, trained on 1M+ clips from 100+ AAA games.
entries.citation: Hunyuan-GameCraft — Li, J. et al. "Hunyuan-GameCraft: High-dynamic Interactive Game Video Generation with Hybrid History Condition." arXiv 2506.17201 (2025).

entries.name: Mirage
entries.fullTitle: Research Preview: The World's First AI-Native UGC Game Engine Powered by Real-Time World Model
entries.description: Real-time transformer-based autoregressive diffusion game engine playable at 16 FPS with frame-level prompt processing, letting players reshape the ongoing world via text, keyboard, or controller mid-rollout. (Unrelated to the §2.4 "Mirage / Latent Spatial Memory" paper.)
entries.citation: Mirage — "Research Preview: The World's First AI-Native UGC Game Engine Powered by Real-Time World Model." Dynamics Lab Blog (2025).

entries.name: ActionSplice
entries.fullTitle: ActionSplice: In-Flight Action Editing for Interactive World Models
entries.description: Edits actions during chunk sampling by transporting intermediate states toward the revised action, supporting whole-chunk retargeting or suffix-only updates without replaying completed sampler steps.
entries.citation: ActionSplice — "ActionSplice: In-Flight Action Editing for Interactive World Models." arXiv 2609.08230 (2026).

entries.name: H3-World
entries.fullTitle: H3-World: Turning Language Understanding into World Control
entries.description: Adapts MiniMax-H3 to interactive character and camera control by expressing actions as temporally aligned language instructions and routing attention to the intended action interval.
entries.citation: H3-World — "H3-World: Turning Language Understanding into World Control." arXiv 2609.01560 (2026).

entries.name: GameWAM
entries.fullTitle: GameWAM: A World Action Model for Video Games
entries.description: Jointly generates future game observations and native keyboard-mouse actions with block-causal flow matching, then executes short action blocks and replans from refreshed observations for gameplay and GUI control.
entries.citation: GameWAM — "GameWAM: A World Action Model for Video Games." arXiv 2608.26200 (2026).

entries.name: Genie
entries.fullTitle: Genie: Generative Interactive Environments
entries.description: One of the most influential post-World-Models papers; learns latent action interfaces from unlabeled internet video to generate controllable 2D environments.
entries.citation: Genie — Bruce, J. et al. "Genie: Generative Interactive Environments." arXiv 2402.15391 (2024).

entries.name: Genie 2
entries.fullTitle: Genie 2
entries.description: Foundation world model generating an endless variety of action-controllable, playable 3D environments from a single image prompt; playable by humans or AI agents.
entries.citation: Genie 2 — Parker-Holder, J. et al. DeepMind Blog (December 2024).

entries.name: Genie 3
entries.fullTitle: Genie 3
entries.description: Real-time text-to-world generation at 24 fps / 720p with minutes of coherent play — a decisive shift from passive video generation to live interactive worlds.
entries.citation: Genie 3 — Ball, P. et al. DeepMind Blog (August 2025).

entries.name: Oasis
entries.fullTitle: Oasis: A Universe in a Transformer
entries.description: Transformer world model generating Minecraft interactively, token by token, without a game engine.
entries.citation: Oasis — "Oasis: A Universe in a Transformer." (2024).

entries.name: MineWorld
entries.fullTitle: MineWorld: a Real-Time and Open-Source Interactive World Model on Minecraft
entries.description: Learns Minecraft transitions with interleaved visual-action tokens and parallel frame decoding for real-time player interaction.
entries.citation: MineWorld — "MineWorld: a Real-Time and Open-Source Interactive World Model on Minecraft." arXiv 2504.08388 (2025).

entries.name: Solaris
entries.fullTitle: Solaris: Building a Multiplayer Video World Model in Minecraft
entries.description: Pushes interactive world modeling from single-player rollouts toward shared multiplayer Minecraft dynamics.
entries.citation: Solaris — "Solaris: Building a Multiplayer Video World Model in Minecraft." arXiv 2602.22208 (2026).

entries.name: GameFactory
entries.fullTitle: GameFactory: Creating New Games with Generative Interactive Videos
entries.description: Generates entirely new game experiences via generative interactive video.
entries.citation: GameFactory — Wen, Y. et al. "GameFactory: Creating New Games with Generative Interactive Videos." arXiv 2501.08325 (2025).

entries.name: AnimeGamer
entries.fullTitle: AnimeGamer: Infinite Anime Life Simulation with Next Game State Prediction
entries.description: Predicts action-aware animation-shot representations and character-state updates from language instructions and historical visual context, then decodes the predicted representations into video for interactive anime simulation.
entries.citation: AnimeGamer — "AnimeGamer: Infinite Anime Life Simulation with Next Game State Prediction." arXiv 2504.01014 (2025).

entries.name: Multiplayer Interactive World Models
entries.fullTitle: Multiplayer Interactive World Models with Representation Autoencoders
entries.description: Models multiple players' action streams jointly in Rocket League, extending interactive world modeling from single-agent control to tightly coupled multiplayer dynamics.
entries.citation: Multiplayer Interactive World Models — "Multiplayer Interactive World Models with Representation Autoencoders." arXiv 2607.05352 (2026).

entries.name: AlayaWorld
entries.fullTitle: AlayaWorld: Long-Horizon and Playable Video World Generation
entries.description: Interactive long-horizon world generation; the full report and v1.1 supplement develop streaming 3D point-cache memory and temporally aligned causal-VAE conditioning for more consistent exploration.
entries.citation: AlayaWorld — "AlayaWorld: Long-Horizon and Playable Video World Generation." arXiv 2607.06291 (2026).

entries.name: Playable Video Generation
entries.fullTitle: Playable Video Generation
entries.description: Learns a discrete latent action space from unlabeled video so a user selects an action at every step of generation — the direct precursor of Genie's latent-action interface.
entries.citation: Playable Video Generation — Menapace, W. et al. "Playable Video Generation." CVPR 2021.

entries.name: Promptable Game Models
entries.fullTitle: Promptable Game Models: Text-Guided Game Simulation via Masked Diffusion Models
entries.description: Represents a game as an environment state evolved by agent actions, adds text-promptable high- and low-level control, and learns an animation "game AI" enabling a goal-directed director's mode.
entries.citation: Promptable Game Models — Menapace, W. et al. "Promptable Game Models: Text-Guided Game Simulation via Masked Diffusion Models." ACM TOG 2023.

entries.name: WHAM / Muse
entries.fullTitle: World and Human Action Models towards gameplay ideation
entries.description: Microsoft's 1.6B autoregressive transformer over tokenized Bleeding Edge visuals and controller actions; runs as a world model, a behavior policy, or both, and persists user mid-sequence edits — open weights plus the WHAM Demonstrator.
entries.citation: WHAM / Muse — Kanervisto, A. et al. "World and Human Action Models towards gameplay ideation." Nature 638 (2025).

entries.name: Jasmine
entries.fullTitle: Jasmine: A Simple, Performant and Scalable JAX-based World Modeling Codebase
entries.description: Open, fully reproducible training infrastructure for Genie-style interactive world models, reproducing the Genie CoinRun case study an order of magnitude faster than prior open implementations. (Could alternatively live under Community Resources → Open Toolkits.)
entries.citation: Jasmine — Mahajan, M. et al. "Jasmine: A Simple, Performant and Scalable JAX-based World Modeling Codebase." arXiv 2510.27002 (2025).

entries.name: ActionParty
entries.fullTitle: ActionParty: Multi-Subject Action Binding in Generative Video Games
entries.description: Introduces persistent subject state tokens that bind each action to its subject, disentangling global frame rendering from per-subject updates; controls up to seven players simultaneously across 46 Melting Pot environments.
entries.citation: ActionParty — Pondaven, A. et al. "ActionParty: Multi-Subject Action Binding in Generative Video Games." ECCV 2026.

entries.name: WanToFight
entries.fullTitle: WanToFight: Real-Time Generative Game Engine for Multi-Player Combat Interaction
entries.description: First generative game engine combining two-player adversarial control, real-time inference, and contact physics: a streaming block-causal DiT with player-association modules binding each keyboard stream to a KOF '97 character at 30 FPS.
entries.citation: WanToFight — Hu, L. et al. "WanToFight: Real-Time Generative Game Engine for Multi-Player Combat Interaction." arXiv 2607.12592 (2026).

entries.name: WorldWeaver (W²)
entries.fullTitle: Streaming Multi-Agent Autoregressive Diffusion Model with World State Registers
entries.description: Augments streaming rollout with learnable cross-agent world-state registers — shared world information and per-agent status updated after every generated chunk — improving logical consistency in two-agent Minecraft. (Distinct from the 1.6 WorldWeaver, 2508.15720.)
entries.citation: WorldWeaver (W²) — Mo, S. et al. "Streaming Multi-Agent Autoregressive Diffusion Model with World State Registers." arXiv 2607.21594 (2026).

entries.name: Odyssey-1 / Odyssey-2
entries.fullTitle: Introducing Odyssey-2: A General-Purpose World Model
entries.description: Frontier-lab playable world models: causal autoregressive frame prediction conditioned on state, action, and history, streaming a new frame every 40–50 ms for multi-minute interactive rollouts steered by text mid-stream.
entries.citation: Odyssey-1 / Odyssey-2 — "Introducing Odyssey-2: A General-Purpose World Model." Odyssey Blog (2026).

entries.name: Oasis 2.0
entries.fullTitle: Oasis 2.0
entries.description: Follow-up to the Oasis entry already in §1.1.2: 1080p/30fps real-time generative Minecraft shipped as a playable mod that restyles and regenerates the live game world frame-by-frame.
entries.citation: Oasis 2.0 — "Oasis 2.0." Decart (2026).

entries.name: Oasis 3
entries.fullTitle: Oasis 3: The Interactive World Model for Physical AI
entries.description: First API-accessible interactive world model: robot/vehicle actions in, multi-camera photorealistic views out, with unbounded-length real-time generation targeted at policy training and evaluation.
entries.citation: Oasis 3 — "Oasis 3: The Interactive World Model for Physical AI." Decart (2026).

entries.name: AlayaVista
entries.fullTitle: AlayaVista: Streaming World Modeling from Panoramic States to Perspective Video
entries.description: Evolves a camera-conditioned panoramic latent world state and renders refined perspective observations for streaming exploration; introduces the MUGEN panoramic video dataset.
entries.citation: AlayaVista — "AlayaVista: Streaming World Modeling from Panoramic States to Perspective Video." arXiv 2609.14462 (2026).

entries.name: World in World
entries.fullTitle: World in World: Explore the World with World Models
entries.description: Training-free control interface routes camera- and time-labelled visual evidence into a frozen causal video model for viewpoint-controlled rerendering, long-horizon revisits, and motion transfer.
entries.citation: World in World — "World in World: Explore the World with World Models." arXiv 2609.11548 (2026).

entries.name: Programmable World Model
entries.fullTitle: Programmable World Model
entries.description: Executes explicit entity-state programs and persistent transition rules, then compiles state-augmented 3D boxes into conditioning for a video renderer; evaluates playable mechanics and off-screen state on CombatStateBench.
entries.citation: Programmable World Model — arXiv 2609.10540 (2026).

entries.name: SolarWM
entries.fullTitle: SolarWM: Open Data and Scalable Training for Long-Horizon Video World Models
entries.description: Open data engine and shared training recipe adapt multiple video backbones into camera-conditioned causal simulators, using unified clips, autoregressive initialization, and distillation for long-horizon interaction.
entries.citation: SolarWM — "SolarWM: Open Data and Scalable Training for Long-Horizon Video World Models." arXiv 2609.02886 (2026).

entries.name: Matrix-Game 3.5
entries.fullTitle: Matrix-Game 3.5: Enhancing Real-Time Streaming Interactive World Models with Patch Memory
entries.description: Combines explicit 3D patch memory and projective camera conditioning with static-dynamic factorization and progressive distillation for long-horizon streaming world generation.
entries.citation: Matrix-Game 3.5 — "Matrix-Game 3.5: Enhancing Real-Time Streaming Interactive World Models with Patch Memory." arXiv 2608.29910 (2026).

entries.name: ABot-World-0
entries.fullTitle: ABot-World-0: Infinite Interactive World Rollout on a Single Desktop GPU
entries.description: Combines keyboard-conditioned causal generation, long-rollout alignment, and character memory for desktop interactive world simulation.
entries.citation: ABot-World-0 — "ABot-World-0: Infinite Interactive World Rollout on a Single Desktop GPU." arXiv 2607.19191 (2026).

entries.name: Wonder
entries.fullTitle: Wonder: Video World Model Done Better
entries.description: General-purpose video world model for real-time, camera-controllable exploration. Uses sparse attention-based memory to support minute-scale interactive rollouts while preserving geometry, appearance, and dynamics.
entries.citation: Wonder — Xu, J. et al. "Wonder: Video World Model Done Better." arXiv 2607.26037 (2026).

entries.name: WorldMem
entries.fullTitle: WorldMem: Long-term Consistent World Simulation with Memory
entries.description: Addresses long-term consistency through an explicit memory module; enables coherent multi-minute gameplay.
entries.citation: WorldMem — "WorldMem: Long-term Consistent World Simulation with Memory." arXiv 2504.12369 (2025).

entries.name: Matrix-Game 3.0
entries.fullTitle: Matrix-Game 3.0: Real-Time and Streaming Interactive World Model with Long-Horizon Memory
entries.description: Extends open interactive world models with real-time streaming and explicit long-horizon memory.
entries.citation: Matrix-Game 3.0 — "Matrix-Game 3.0: Real-Time and Streaming Interactive World Model with Long-Horizon Memory." arXiv 2604.08995 (2026).

entries.name: WorldCam
entries.fullTitle: WorldCam: Interactive Autoregressive 3D Gaming Worlds with Camera Pose as a Unifying Geometric Representation
entries.description: Brings 3D camera geometry into game-world autoregression for more stable interactive navigation.
entries.citation: WorldCam — "WorldCam: Interactive Autoregressive 3D Gaming Worlds with Camera Pose as a Unifying Geometric Representation." arXiv 2603.16871 (2026).

entries.name: MagicWorld
entries.fullTitle: MagicWorld: Towards Long-Horizon Stability for Interactive Video World Exploration
entries.description: Stabilizes long interactive video rollouts with flow-guided motion preservation, retrieval from a history cache, and multi-shot aggregated distillation; introduces the RealWM120K city-walk dataset.
entries.citation: MagicWorld — "MagicWorld: Towards Long-Horizon Stability for Interactive Video World Exploration." arXiv 2511.18886 (2025).

entries.name: LIVE
entries.fullTitle: LIVE: Long-horizon Interactive Video World Modeling
entries.description: Focuses directly on long-horizon interactive consistency, a core bottleneck for usable video world models.
entries.citation: LIVE — "LIVE: Long-horizon Interactive Video World Modeling." arXiv 2602.03747 (2026).

entries.name: Infinite-World
entries.fullTitle: Infinite-World: Scaling Interactive World Models to 1000-Frame Horizons via Pose-Free Hierarchical Memory
entries.description: Pushes interactive world models to 1000+ frame horizons with pose-free hierarchical memory, targeting real-world long-term consistency beyond short synthetic rollouts.
entries.citation: Infinite-World — "Infinite-World: Scaling Interactive World Models to 1000-Frame Horizons via Pose-Free Hierarchical Memory." arXiv 2602.02393 (2026).

entries.name: SANA-WM
entries.fullTitle: SANA-WM: Efficient Minute-Scale World Modeling with Hybrid Linear Diffusion Transformer
entries.description: Open 2.6B minute-scale video world model with 720p generation and 6-DoF camera control.
entries.citation: SANA-WM — "SANA-WM: Efficient Minute-Scale World Modeling with Hybrid Linear Diffusion Transformer." arXiv 2605.15178 (2026).

entries.name: minWM
entries.fullTitle: minWM: A Full-Stack Open-Source Framework for Real-Time Interactive Video World Models
entries.description: Converts bidirectional T2V/TI2V video foundation models into controllable, causal, few-step autoregressive world models for low-latency interaction.
entries.citation: minWM — "minWM: A Full-Stack Open-Source Framework for Real-Time Interactive Video World Models." arXiv 2605.30263 (2026).

entries.name: DreamForge-World 0.1
entries.fullTitle: DreamForge-World 0.1 Preview: A Low-Compute Real-Time Controllable World Model
entries.description: A low-compute interactive world-model preview supporting keyboard/mouse control, multimodal initialization, reprompting, and minute-scale rollouts on consumer GPUs.
entries.citation: DreamForge-World 0.1 — "DreamForge-World 0.1 Preview: A Low-Compute Real-Time Controllable World Model." arXiv 2606.30292 (2026).

entries.name: WorldDirector
entries.fullTitle: WorldDirector: Building Controllable World Simulators with Persistent Dynamic Memory
entries.description: Decouples semantic motion orchestration from video generation to support controllable simulators with persistent dynamic-object memory and unrestricted viewpoint exploration.
entries.citation: WorldDirector — "WorldDirector: Building Controllable World Simulators with Persistent Dynamic Memory." arXiv 2607.02517 (2026).

entries.name: MemLearner
entries.fullTitle: MemLearner: Learning to Query Context Memory for Video World Models
entries.description: Learns adaptive context queries for long-horizon video world models, targeting scene consistency under occlusion and dynamic-object changes.
entries.citation: MemLearner — "MemLearner: Learning to Query Context Memory for Video World Models." arXiv 2606.31734 (2026).

entries.name: DreamX-World 1.0
entries.fullTitle: DreamX-World 1.0: A General-Purpose Interactive World Model
entries.description: General-purpose interactive world model with camera control, geometry-guided memory retrieval, promptable events, and efficient long-horizon rollouts.
entries.citation: DreamX-World 1.0 — "DreamX-World 1.0: A General-Purpose Interactive World Model." arXiv 2606.16993 (2026).

entries.name: From Zero to Hero / SPAWN
entries.fullTitle: From Zero to Hero: Training-Free Custom Concept Spawning in World Models
entries.description: Adds training-free concept spawning for autoregressive interactive world models, improving user control over unseen regions.
entries.citation: From Zero to Hero / SPAWN — "From Zero to Hero: Training-Free Custom Concept Spawning in World Models." arXiv 2606.02575 (2026).

entries.name: SCOPE
entries.fullTitle: SCOPE: Simulating Cross-game Operations in Playable Environments for FPS World Models
entries.description: Expands playable FPS world models toward cross-game operation and transfer rather than one-map imitation.
entries.citation: SCOPE — "SCOPE: Simulating Cross-game Operations in Playable Environments for FPS World Models." arXiv 2605.23345 (2026).

entries.name: WorldCraft
entries.fullTitle: WorldCraft: From Camera Navigation to Object Manipulation in Interactive Video World Models
entries.description: Focuses on controllable creation and editing of interactive worlds rather than passive action-conditioned playback.
entries.citation: WorldCraft — "WorldCraft: From Camera Navigation to Object Manipulation in Interactive Video World Models." arXiv 2605.25077 (2026).

entries.name: DecMem
entries.fullTitle: DecMem: Towards Minute-Long Consistent World Generation with Decoupled Memory
entries.description: Separates short-term and long-term memory for minute-scale world generation consistency.
entries.citation: DecMem — "DecMem: Towards Minute-Long Consistent World Generation with Decoupled Memory." arXiv 2605.31336 (2026).

entries.name: GIM-World
entries.fullTitle: Geometry-Aware Implicit Memory for Video World Models
entries.description: Adds geometry-aware implicit memory to improve spatial consistency in video world rollouts.
entries.citation: GIM-World — "Geometry-Aware Implicit Memory for Video World Models." arXiv 2606.02436 (2026).

entries.name: ActWorld
entries.fullTitle: ActWorld: From Explorable to Interactive World Model via Action-Aware Memory
entries.description: Moves beyond navigation-only exploration by supporting mid-rollout object interaction through hierarchical action-aware memory.
entries.citation: ActWorld — "ActWorld: From Explorable to Interactive World Model via Action-Aware Memory." arXiv 2606.17730 (2026).

entries.name: RealPlay
entries.fullTitle: From Virtual Games to Real-World Play
entries.description: Bridges game-world training and real-world embodied play through shared world representations.
entries.citation: RealPlay — "From Virtual Games to Real-World Play." arXiv 2506.18901 (2025).

entries.name: Unbounded
entries.fullTitle: Unbounded: A Generative Infinite Game of Character Life Simulation
entries.description: Tracks a set of character attributes (hunger, energy, fun, hygiene) plus the current environment and interaction history across game turns, updates them with a distilled real-time LLM game engine in response to open-ended player actions, and renders each turn with regionally consistent image generation, yielding an open-ended playable character-life simulation.
entries.citation: Unbounded — "Unbounded: A Generative Infinite Game of Character Life Simulation." arXiv 2410.18975 (2024).

entries.name: Waypoint-1
entries.fullTitle: The Path to Real-Time Worlds and Why It Matters
entries.citation: Waypoint-1 — "The Path to Real-Time Worlds and Why It Matters." Over.world Blog (2025).

entries.name: StatePlay
entries.fullTitle: StatePlay: State-Aware Game World Models for Mechanics-Consistent Generation
entries.description: Jointly predicts visual content and explicit game states such as health points, skill meters, and timers, allowing predicted states to guide frame generation and improve mechanics consistency.
entries.citation: StatePlay — Lin, Z. et al. "StatePlay: State-Aware Game World Models for Mechanics-Consistent Generation." arXiv 2607.26754 (2026).

entries.name: ActSWM
entries.fullTitle: ActSWM: Action-Sensitive World Models for Long-Horizon Planning in Open-World Games
entries.description: Enforces transition separation in autoregressive latent rollouts so that alternative-action futures remain distinguishable, improving long-horizon planning and action recovery in Minecraft and other games.
entries.citation: ActSWM — Gan, Z. et al. "ActSWM: Action-Sensitive World Models for Long-Horizon Planning in Open-World Games." arXiv 2607.26712 (2026).

entries.name: EDELINE
entries.fullTitle: EDELINE: Enhancing Memory in Diffusion-based World Models via Linear-Time Sequence Modeling
entries.description: Direct DIAMOND follow-up: unifies state-space sequence models with diffusion world models to lift the fixed-context memory limit, improving RL agents on Atari-100k, memory-demanding Crafter, and ViZDoom.
entries.citation: EDELINE — Lee, J.-H. et al. "EDELINE: Enhancing Memory in Diffusion-based World Models via Linear-Time Sequence Modeling." arXiv 2502.00466 (2025).

entries.name: Yume
entries.fullTitle: Yume: An Interactive World Generation Model
entries.description: Creates an explorable dynamic world from one image with quantized keyboard camera actions and a Masked Video Diffusion Transformer carrying a memory module for infinite autoregressive rollouts.
entries.citation: Yume — Mao, X. et al. "Yume: An Interactive World Generation Model." arXiv 2507.17744 (2025).

entries.name: Memory Forcing
entries.fullTitle: Memory Forcing: Spatio-Temporal Memory for Consistent Scene Generation on Minecraft
entries.description: Pairs hybrid/chained-rollout training with geometry-indexed spatial memory (point-to-frame retrieval over an incrementally reconstructed 3D cache) so Minecraft rollouts explore freely yet stay consistent on revisits.
entries.citation: Memory Forcing — Huang, J. et al. "Memory Forcing: Spatio-Temporal Memory for Consistent Scene Generation on Minecraft." arXiv 2510.03198 (2025).

entries.name: RELIC
entries.fullTitle: RELIC: Interactive Video World Model with Long-Horizon Memory
entries.description: 14B real-time (16 FPS) interactive model storing the entire history as highly compressed camera-aware latent tokens in the KV cache, trained with a memory-efficient self-forcing paradigm for full-context distillation over long rollouts.
entries.citation: RELIC — Hong, Y. et al. "RELIC: Interactive Video World Model with Long-Horizon Memory." arXiv 2512.04040 (2025).

entries.name: WorldPlay
entries.fullTitle: WorldPlay: Towards Long-Term Geometric Consistency for Real-Time Interactive World Modeling
entries.description: Tencent's streaming world model with dual action representation, reconstituted context memory (temporal reframing keeps geometrically important past frames addressable), and memory-aligned "context forcing" distillation for 720p/24 FPS rollouts.
entries.citation: WorldPlay — Sun, W. et al. "WorldPlay: Towards Long-Term Geometric Consistency for Real-Time Interactive World Modeling." arXiv 2512.14614 (2025).

entries.name: Yume-1.5
entries.fullTitle: Yume-1.5: A Text-Controlled Interactive World Generation Model
entries.description: Adds unified context compression with linear attention, bidirectional-attention distillation for real-time streaming, and text-controlled in-world events to the Yume line of keyboard-explorable worlds.
entries.citation: Yume-1.5 — Mao, X. et al. "Yume-1.5: A Text-Controlled Interactive World Generation Model." arXiv 2512.22096 (2025).

entries.name: MultiGen
entries.fullTitle: MultiGen: Level-Design for Editable Multiplayer Worlds in Diffusion Game Engines
entries.description: Decomposes the diffusion game engine into Memory/Observation/Dynamics modules around a persistent, user-editable external memory, enabling reproducible level design and coherent real-time multiplayer rollouts.
entries.citation: MultiGen — Po, R. et al. "MultiGen: Level-Design for Editable Multiplayer Worlds in Diffusion Game Engines." arXiv 2603.06679 (2026).

entries.name: Incantation
entries.fullTitle: Incantation: Natural Language as the Action Interface for Multi-Entity Video World Models
entries.description: Per-latent-frame (0.25 s) natural-language action conditioning gives simultaneous multi-entity control and cross-entity concept transfer in Elden Ring and KOF worlds, streaming at 19.7 FPS with stable two-hour rollouts.
entries.citation: Incantation — Zhu, S. et al. "Incantation: Natural Language as the Action Interface for Multi-Entity Video World Models." arXiv 2605.18601 (2026).

entries.name: LingBot-World 2.0
entries.fullTitle: Infinite Worlds with Versatile Interactions
entries.description: Open interactive world model with unbounded interaction horizon via causal pretraining, a 60 fps/720p real-time distilled variant, rich action and text-event interfaces, a pilot/director agentic harness, and a multiplayer interface. (LingBot-World v1 already appears under Open Toolkits.)
entries.citation: LingBot-World 2.0 — Gao, Z. et al. "Infinite Worlds with Versatile Interactions." arXiv 2607.07534 (2026).

entries.name: AlayaRenderer-Flash
entries.fullTitle: Generative World Renderer at the Speed of Play
entries.description: Few-step autoregressive streaming renderer that synthesizes RGB from structured physics-engine world states at 31.5 FPS, composing with a real engine into a fully playable generative world where dynamics live in explicit state.
entries.citation: AlayaRenderer-Flash — Lin, G. et al. "Generative World Renderer at the Speed of Play." arXiv 2607.18703 (2026).

entries.name: HelloWorld
entries.fullTitle: HelloWorld: Enabling Socially Interactive Characters in Video World Models
entries.description: Adds button-press social interventions on in-world characters during an ongoing rollout, using self-distilled interaction data and press-window cross-attention masking to localize the character's response in time.
entries.citation: HelloWorld — Ouyang, L. et al. "HelloWorld: Enabling Socially Interactive Characters in Video World Models." arXiv 2608.05070 (2026).

entries.name: Alaya-EVOKE
entries.fullTitle: Alaya-EVOKE: From Linear-Scaling Supervision to Endless World
entries.description: Externalizes persistent world state into a camera-indexed bank with view-relevant retrieval and redesigns the teacher for linear-scaling long-horizon supervision, yielding a 3-step student supporting open-ended, prompt/event-controllable generation.
entries.citation: Alaya-EVOKE — Yin, Y. et al. "Alaya-EVOKE: From Linear-Scaling Supervision to Endless World." arXiv 2608.13546 (2026).

entries.name: Marionette
entries.fullTitle: Marionette: Predicting World States, Rendering Geometry, Painting Appearance
entries.description: Autoregressively predicts an explicit, interpretable 276-dim 3D world state (articulated skeletons, metric trajectories), renders geometry with a zero-parameter graphics bridge, and paints appearance with control-conditioned diffusion — long-horizon behavior can be repaired by rules imposed directly on the state.
entries.citation: Marionette — Meng, Z. et al. "Marionette: Predicting World States, Rendering Geometry, Painting Appearance." arXiv 2608.14530 (2026).

entries.name: WorldMind
entries.fullTitle: WorldMind: Decoupled Game World Model for State-Aware NPC Behavior
entries.description: Decouples interactive world modeling into understanding/decision/control/generation layers reconnected in a closed loop, grounding NPC actions in an explicit compact game state; ships the BOSS-140K gameplay+state dataset.
entries.citation: WorldMind — Deng, Z. et al. "WorldMind: Decoupled Game World Model for State-Aware NPC Behavior." arXiv 2608.21439 (2026).

entries.name: ReWorld
entries.fullTitle: ReWorld: An Interactive World Model with Long-Horizon Memory
entries.description: Separates control (windowed heads) from memory (global heads over a bounded, pose-indexed landmark KV bank) with a metric-scale-aligned data engine; regenerates the starting view after minute-long out-and-back rollouts where sliding windows have evicted the evidence.
entries.citation: ReWorld — Chen, Z. et al. "ReWorld: An Interactive World Model with Long-Horizon Memory." arXiv 2608.23565 (2026).

entries.name: SimGen
entries.fullTitle: SimGen: Simulator-conditioned Driving Scene Generation
entries.description: Conditions scene generation on simulator layouts and real-world driving data to bridge visual domain gaps and synthesize safety-critical scenarios.
entries.citation: SimGen — "SimGen: Simulator-conditioned Driving Scene Generation." arXiv 2406.09386 (2024).

entries.name: Unleashing Generalization of End-to-End Autonomous Driving with Controllable Long Video Generation
entries.fullTitle: Unleashing Generalization of End-to-End Autonomous Driving with Controllable Long Video Generation
entries.description: Generates controllable long multi-view driving videos and targets failure cases to improve end-to-end driving planning.
entries.citation: Unleashing Generalization of End-to-End Autonomous Driving with Controllable Long Video Generation — arXiv 2406.01349 (2024).

entries.name: SubjectDrive
entries.fullTitle: SubjectDrive: Scaling Generative Data in Autonomous Driving via Subject Control
entries.description: Adds subject control to driving data generation to improve synthetic-data diversity for downstream perception.
entries.citation: SubjectDrive — "SubjectDrive: Scaling Generative Data in Autonomous Driving via Subject Control." arXiv 2403.19438 (2024).

entries.name: DrivingDiffusion
entries.fullTitle: DrivingDiffusion: Layout-Guided multi-view driving scene video generation with latent diffusion model
entries.description: Generates temporally consistent multi-camera driving videos conditioned on 3D layouts for synthetic driving data.
entries.citation: DrivingDiffusion — "DrivingDiffusion: Layout-Guided multi-view driving scene video generation with latent diffusion model." arXiv 2310.07771 (2023).

entries.name: GAIA-1
entries.fullTitle: GAIA-1: A Generative World Model for Autonomous Driving
entries.description: Models tokenized video, text, and actions autoregressively to generate driving scenes with control over ego-vehicle behavior and scene attributes.
entries.citation: GAIA-1 — Hu, A. et al. "GAIA-1: A Generative World Model for Autonomous Driving." Wayve (2023).

entries.name: GAIA-2
entries.fullTitle: GAIA-2: A Controllable Multi-View Generative World Model for Autonomous Driving
entries.description: Multi-view extension with fine-grained controllability over agent behaviors and scene attributes.
entries.citation: GAIA-2 — "GAIA-2: A Controllable Multi-View Generative World Model for Autonomous Driving." arXiv 2503.20523 (2025).

entries.name: Xiaomi Auto World Model
entries.fullTitle: Xiaomi Auto World Model: A Joint World Model Integrating Reconstruction and Generation for Autonomous Driving
entries.description: Integrates feed-forward 3D Gaussian reconstruction with online causal video generation for closed-loop simulation and data synthesis.
entries.citation: Xiaomi Auto World Model — "Xiaomi Auto World Model: A Joint World Model Integrating Reconstruction and Generation for Autonomous Driving." arXiv 2605.18137 (2026).

entries.name: Drive-WM
entries.fullTitle: Driving into the Future: Multiview Visual Forecasting and Planning with World Model for Autonomous Driving
entries.description: One of the early representative driving world models that tightly couples future visual forecasting and planning.
entries.citation: Drive-WM — "Driving into the Future: Multiview Visual Forecasting and Planning with World Model for Autonomous Driving." CVPR 2024.

entries.name: DriveDreamer
entries.fullTitle: DriveDreamer: Towards Real-world-driven World Models for Autonomous Driving
entries.description: Learns structured traffic constraints and future driving states through a two-stage diffusion training pipeline, supporting controllable driving-video generation and driving-policy generation from real-world data.
entries.citation: DriveDreamer — "DriveDreamer: Towards Real-world-driven World Models for Autonomous Driving." ECCV 2024.

entries.name: MagicDrive
entries.fullTitle: MagicDrive: Street View Generation with Diverse 3D Geometry Control
entries.description: A widely cited controllable street-scene generation baseline close to practical driving world modeling.
entries.citation: MagicDrive — "MagicDrive: Street View Generation with Diverse 3D Geometry Control." ICLR 2024.

entries.name: DriveDreamer-2
entries.fullTitle: DriveDreamer-2: LLM-Enhanced World Models for Diverse Driving Video Generation
entries.description: Adds language-enhanced control for more diverse and editable driving rollouts.
entries.citation: DriveDreamer-2 — "DriveDreamer-2: LLM-Enhanced World Models for Diverse Driving Video Generation." arXiv 2403.06845 (2024).

entries.name: Vista
entries.fullTitle: Vista: A Generalizable Driving World Model with High Fidelity and Versatile Controllability
entries.description: A strong 2024 driving baseline with a good balance of fidelity, control, and downstream usefulness.
entries.citation: Vista — "Vista: A Generalizable Driving World Model with High Fidelity and Versatile Controllability." NeurIPS 2024.

entries.name: Cosmos-Drive-Dreams
entries.fullTitle: Cosmos-Drive-Dreams: Scalable Synthetic Driving Data Generation with World Foundation Models
entries.description: NVIDIA's Cosmos-based large-scale synthetic data pipeline for autonomous driving.
entries.citation: Cosmos-Drive-Dreams — "Cosmos-Drive-Dreams: Scalable Synthetic Driving Data Generation with World Foundation Models." arXiv 2506.09042 (2025).

entries.name: NVIDIA OmniDreams
entries.fullTitle: NVIDIA OmniDreams: Real-Time Generative World Model for Closed-Loop Autonomous Vehicle Simulation
entries.description: Cosmos-based real-time, action-conditioned driving simulator for closed-loop policy evaluation under novel weather, traffic, and long-tail dynamics.
entries.citation: NVIDIA OmniDreams — "NVIDIA OmniDreams: Real-Time Generative World Model for Closed-Loop Autonomous Vehicle Simulation." arXiv 2606.03159 (2026).

entries.name: OmniDrive
entries.fullTitle: OmniDrive: An LLM-Choreographed Multi-Agent World Model with Unified Latent Co-Compression for Multi-View Driving Video Generation
entries.description: Uses LLM agents as a symbolic control interlingua for view-consistent, multi-agent driving video generation.
entries.citation: OmniDrive — "OmniDrive: An LLM-Choreographed Multi-Agent World Model with Unified Latent Co-Compression for Multi-View Driving Video Generation." arXiv 2606.17536 (2026).

entries.name: GEM
entries.fullTitle: GEM: A Generalizable Ego-Vision Multimodal World Model for Fine-Grained Ego-Motion, Object Dynamics, and Scene Composition Control
entries.description: Predicts paired RGB and depth futures conditioned on reference frames, sparse features, human poses, and ego-trajectories, with autoregressive noise schedules for long-horizon control of ego-motion and object dynamics.
entries.citation: GEM — "GEM: A Generalizable Ego-Vision Multimodal World Model for Fine-Grained Ego-Motion, Object Dynamics, and Scene Composition Control." arXiv 2412.11198 (2024).

entries.name: MAD
entries.fullTitle: MAD: Motion Appearance Decoupling for efficient Driving World Models
entries.description: Separates motion learning from appearance rendering — a useful efficiency recipe for controllable driving rollouts.
entries.citation: MAD — "MAD: Motion Appearance Decoupling for efficient Driving World Models." arXiv 2601.09452 (2026).

entries.name: ReconDreamer
entries.fullTitle: ReconDreamer: Crafting World Models for Driving Scene Reconstruction via Online Restoration
entries.description: Integrates world-model priors into driving-scene reconstruction through online artifact restoration and progressive data updates, improving rendering along novel trajectories and large lane-change maneuvers.
entries.citation: ReconDreamer — "ReconDreamer: Crafting World Models for Driving Scene Reconstruction via Online Restoration." arXiv 2411.19548 (2024).

entries.name: InfinityDrive
entries.fullTitle: InfinityDrive: Breaking Time Limits in Driving World Models
entries.description: Combines spatiotemporal modeling, extended temporal training, and memory injection and retention with an adaptive memory loss to reduce accumulated errors in long driving-video rollouts.
entries.citation: InfinityDrive — "InfinityDrive: Breaking Time Limits in Driving World Models." arXiv 2412.01522 (2024).

entries.name: LongDWM
entries.fullTitle: LongDWM: Cross-Granularity Distillation for Building a Long-Term Driving World Model
entries.description: Decouples large-motion and continuous-motion learning and distills fine-grained video flows into coarse-grained flows to improve temporal coherence in long driving-world-model rollouts.
entries.citation: LongDWM — "LongDWM: Cross-Granularity Distillation for Building a Long-Term Driving World Model." arXiv 2506.01546 (2025).

entries.name: Out of Sight but Not Out of Mind
entries.fullTitle: Out of Sight but Not Out of Mind: Hybrid Memory for Dynamic Video World Models
entries.description: A recent memory-centric update for preserving off-screen dynamics in long driving rollouts.
entries.citation: Out of Sight but Not Out of Mind — "Out of Sight but Not Out of Mind: Hybrid Memory for Dynamic Video World Models." arXiv 2603.25716 (2026).

entries.name: MiLA
entries.fullTitle: MiLA: Multi-view Intensive-fidelity Long-term Video Generation World Model for Autonomous Driving
entries.description: Uses coarse-to-refine generation, a temporal progressive denoising schedule, and joint denoising and correction to reduce dynamic-object distortions and accumulated errors in long multi-view driving videos.
entries.citation: MiLA — "MiLA: Multi-view Intensive-fidelity Long-term Video Generation World Model for Autonomous Driving." arXiv 2503.15875 (2025).

entries.name: PosePilot
entries.fullTitle: PosePilot: Steering Camera Pose for Generative World Models with Self-supervised Depth
entries.description: Adds self-supervised depth and camera-pose readouts, pose-aware frame warping, and geometric losses to improve camera-pose control in diffusion and autoregressive world models.
entries.citation: PosePilot — "PosePilot: Steering Camera Pose for Generative World Models with Self-supervised Depth." arXiv 2505.01729 (2025).

entries.name: DiST-4D
entries.fullTitle: DiST-4D: Disentangled Spatiotemporal Diffusion with Metric Depth for 4D Driving Scene Generation
entries.citation: DiST-4D — "DiST-4D: Disentangled Spatiotemporal Diffusion with Metric Depth for 4D Driving Scene Generation." ICCV 2025.

entries.name: DriveDreamer4D
entries.fullTitle: DriveDreamer4D: World Models Are Effective Data Machines for 4D Driving Scene Representation
entries.citation: DriveDreamer4D — "DriveDreamer4D: World Models Are Effective Data Machines for 4D Driving Scene Representation." arXiv 2410.13571 (2024).

entries.name: SimWorld
entries.fullTitle: SimWorld: A Unified Benchmark for Simulator-Conditioned Scene Generation via World Model
entries.citation: SimWorld — "SimWorld: A Unified Benchmark for Simulator-Conditioned Scene Generation via World Model." arXiv 2503.13952 (2025).

entries.name: UniFuture
entries.fullTitle: UniFuture: A 4D Driving World Model for Future Generation and Perception
entries.citation: UniFuture — "UniFuture: A 4D Driving World Model for Future Generation and Perception." ICRA 2026.

entries.name: UniDriveDreamer
entries.fullTitle: UniDriveDreamer: A Single-Stage Multimodal World Model for Autonomous Driving
entries.description: Unifies multi-camera video and LiDAR generation in a single-stage multimodal driving world model.
entries.citation: UniDriveDreamer — "UniDriveDreamer: A Single-Stage Multimodal World Model for Autonomous Driving." arXiv 2602.02002 (2026).

entries.name: STAGE
entries.fullTitle: STAGE: A Stream-Centric Generative World Model for Long-Horizon Driving-Scene Simulation
entries.citation: STAGE — "STAGE: A Stream-Centric Generative World Model for Long-Horizon Driving-Scene Simulation." arXiv 2506.13138 (2025).

entries.name: ReSim
entries.fullTitle: ReSim: Reliable World Simulation for Autonomous Driving
entries.citation: ReSim — "ReSim: Reliable World Simulation for Autonomous Driving." arXiv 2506.09981 (2025).

entries.name: DriVerse
entries.fullTitle: DriVerse: Navigation World Model for Driving Simulation via Multimodal Trajectory Prompting and Motion Alignment
entries.citation: DriVerse — "DriVerse: Navigation World Model for Driving Simulation via Multimodal Trajectory Prompting and Motion Alignment." arXiv 2504.18576 (2025).

entries.name: Epona
entries.fullTitle: Epona: Autoregressive Diffusion World Model for Autonomous Driving
entries.citation: Epona — "Epona: Autoregressive Diffusion World Model for Autonomous Driving." arXiv 2506.24113 (2025).

entries.name: MaskGWM
entries.fullTitle: MaskGWM: A Generalizable Driving World Model with Video Mask Reconstruction
entries.citation: MaskGWM — "MaskGWM: A Generalizable Driving World Model with Video Mask Reconstruction." arXiv 2502.11663 (2025).

entries.name: ResWorld
entries.fullTitle: ResWorld: Temporal Residual World Model for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
entries.description: Introduces residual temporal modeling for end-to-end driving, targeting better long-range rollout stability.
entries.citation: ResWorld — "ResWorld: Temporal Residual World Model for End-to-End Autonomous Driving." arXiv 2602.10884 (2026).

entries.name: Dreamland
entries.fullTitle: Dreamland: Controllable World Creation with Simulator and Generative Models
entries.citation: Dreamland — "Dreamland: Controllable World Creation with Simulator and Generative Models." arXiv 2506.08006 (2025).

entries.name: X-World
entries.fullTitle: X-World: Controllable Ego-Centric Multi-Camera World Models for Scalable End-to-End Driving
entries.description: Recent large-scale multi-camera driving world model with strong controllability emphasis.
entries.citation: X-World — "X-World: Controllable Ego-Centric Multi-Camera World Models for Scalable End-to-End Driving." arXiv 2603.19979 (2026).

entries.name: InfiniCube
entries.fullTitle: InfiniCube: Unbounded and Controllable Dynamic 3D Driving Scene Generation with World-Guided Video Models
entries.citation: InfiniCube — "InfiniCube: Unbounded and Controllable Dynamic 3D Driving Scene Generation with World-Guided Video Models." arXiv 2412.03934 (2024).

entries.name: Physical Informed Driving WM
entries.fullTitle: Physical Informed Driving World Model
entries.citation: Physical Informed Driving WM — "Physical Informed Driving World Model." arXiv 2412.08410 (2024).

entries.name: GenAD (OpenDriveLab)
entries.fullTitle: GenAD: Generalized Predictive Model for Autonomous Driving
entries.description: Large-scale video prediction model trained on ~2000 hours of web driving videos (OpenDV-2K); zero-shot generalization to unseen scenes and action-conditioned prediction.
entries.citation: GenAD (OpenDriveLab) — "GenAD: Generalized Predictive Model for Autonomous Driving." CVPR 2024 Highlight.

entries.name: DriveGAN
entries.fullTitle: DriveGAN: Towards a Controllable High-Quality Neural Simulation
entries.description: Early action-conditioned neural driving simulator learned directly in pixel space from unannotated videos; a pre-diffusion classic of controllable driving simulation.
entries.citation: DriveGAN — "DriveGAN: Towards a Controllable High-Quality Neural Simulation." CVPR 2021.

entries.name: UniSim (Waabi)
entries.fullTitle: UniSim: A Neural Closed-Loop Sensor Simulator
entries.description: Reconstructs logged drives into an editable neural closed-loop simulator that re-renders camera and LiDAR under new ego actions and actor behaviors. Distinct from the identically named UniSim (2310.06114) in §1.3.2.
entries.citation: UniSim (Waabi) — "UniSim: A Neural Closed-Loop Sensor Simulator." CVPR 2023 Highlight.

entries.name: Panacea
entries.fullTitle: Panacea: Panoramic and Controllable Video Generation for Autonomous Driving
entries.description: Generates BEV-layout-controlled panoramic multi-view driving videos for annotation-aligned data augmentation.
entries.citation: Panacea — "Panacea: Panoramic and Controllable Video Generation for Autonomous Driving." CVPR 2024.

entries.name: WoVoGen
entries.fullTitle: WoVoGen: World Volume-aware Diffusion for Controllable Multi-camera Driving Scene Generation
entries.description: Uses an explicit predicted 4D world volume as a prior to keep multi-camera video generation cross-view and temporally consistent.
entries.citation: WoVoGen — "WoVoGen: World Volume-aware Diffusion for Controllable Multi-camera Driving Scene Generation." ECCV 2024.

entries.name: DriveArena
entries.fullTitle: DriveArena: A Closed-loop Generative Simulation Platform for Autonomous Driving
entries.description: Closed-loop generative simulation platform coupling a traffic manager with a conditional world model so driving agents can be evaluated interactively on realistic imagery.
entries.citation: DriveArena — "DriveArena: A Closed-loop Generative Simulation Platform for Autonomous Driving." arXiv 2408.00415 (2024).

entries.name: DrivingDojo
entries.fullTitle: DrivingDojo Dataset: Advancing Interactive and Knowledge-Enriched Driving World Model
entries.description: Dataset built specifically for training interactive driving world models, with dense ego actions, multi-agent interplay, and rare-event clips; also defines an action-instruction-following benchmark.
entries.citation: DrivingDojo — "DrivingDojo Dataset: Advancing Interactive and Knowledge-Enriched Driving World Model." NeurIPS 2024 D&B.

entries.name: MagicDrive-V2
entries.fullTitle: MagicDrive-V2: High-Resolution Long Video Generation for Autonomous Driving with Adaptive Control
entries.description: Scales the MagicDrive line to high-resolution, minute-scale multi-view driving video with geometric control via a DiT backbone.
entries.citation: MagicDrive-V2 — "MagicDrive-V2: High-Resolution Long Video Generation for Autonomous Driving with Adaptive Control." arXiv 2411.13807 (2024).

entries.name: ProphetDWM
entries.fullTitle: ProphetDWM: A Driving World Model for Rolling Out Future Actions and Videos
entries.description: Jointly rolls out future actions and future video, linking action prediction and video generation in one driving world model.
entries.citation: ProphetDWM — "ProphetDWM: A Driving World Model for Rolling Out Future Actions and Videos." arXiv 2505.18650 (2025).

entries.name: World Engine
entries.fullTitle: World Engine: Towards the Era of Post-Training for Autonomous Driving
entries.description: Uses generative world simulation to synthesize safety-critical long-tail interactions at scale for post-training end-to-end driving policies.
entries.citation: World Engine — "World Engine: Towards the Era of Post-Training for Autonomous Driving." arXiv 2606.19836 (2026).

entries.name: CausalDrive
entries.fullTitle: CausalDrive: Real-time Causal World Models for Autonomous Driving
entries.description: Real-time interactive driving simulator with reactive background agents, addressing the non-reactivity of layout-conditioned renderers and the weak semantic control of pure action-conditioned predictors.
entries.citation: CausalDrive — "CausalDrive: Real-time Causal World Models for Autonomous Driving." arXiv 2606.15341 (2026).

entries.name: CVD-STORM
